rationale:
Evidence: the only raced telemetry for the current baseline is iteration 2 (kp 2.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.25, base 1.5, sensors at y 0.05 with x from -0.02 to 0.02). All 60 trials went off_track with zero finishes. Score rose from 59.3 to 64.1 when kp fell from 3.0 to 2.0 and kd rose, but max_error stayed at 0.063 to 0.066, just past the 0.06 m limit (the limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which is 0.06 for every allowed body width). Oscillation is 0.11 to 0.16 and line-loss events are 1 to 2 per run.

Critique points accepted: (a) The draft changed five things at once, so its result could not be attributed. I now make one controller-free change: I return to the iteration 2 controller exactly (kp 2.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.25, base_speed 1.5) and change only the sensing, so the next race isolates whether sensor placement moves max_error. (b) Cutting base_speed to 1.3 would lower the average speed needed for completion, which the critique rightly flags as contradictory, so base_speed stays at 1.5. (c) The 0.015 m spacing left 3 mm gaps between 12 mm footprints. I use 0.012 m spacing, so adjacent footprints abut and the signal has no dead zones. (d) ki = 0.05 is nearly inert, so I keep it unchanged and credit it with no effect. (e) The lower kp of 1.2 extrapolated from the draft is not supported by the data, which shows only a small max_error change for a large kp change, so I do not adopt it.

Critique points partly rejected: the forward move is retained as a test of the sensor-lag hypothesis, but I place the sensors at y = 0.06, not 0.07. This gives about 1 cm more look-ahead than the iteration 2 layout while limiting the overshoot risk the critique raised on tight bends. The span widens from 0.04 m to 0.048 m (x = -0.024 to +0.024), which keeps the outer sensors on the tape at larger errors without adding gaps.

Changes from iteration 2: sensor y 0.05 to 0.06; sensor x span 0.04 m to 0.048 m at 0.012 m spacing. Controller and wheel geometry are unchanged.

Expected result: max_error below 0.06 on at least the oval, with line_loss_events at 0 to 1 and steering_oscillation at or below 0.11. Success threshold: any finish, or progress above 0.25 on all three tracks. If max_error does not fall, the next step is to test kp 1.7 with this sensor layout held fixed, rather than changing sensing again.
